speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Broth, Master Shakespeare. The jaw is not invited to a crust this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is tender, Mistress. Quiet was yesterday. Today I will not pretend it is healed.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf is a penny, and it is a full thumb short of the notch. The soft side is cut.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I see it. I will take the soft side again, and I will call that enough.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence is the board, as it was yesterday. You are out of the house before eleven. I have your cloak off the peg.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not in the afternoon play. The Shrew can shift without me. I shall be home when it is up, and out again at five.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The hem has Saturday's mud on it still. Turn, and I will brush it before you go.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Brush it, Alse. I am going among men who look at a leg before they look at a play.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Men who look at legs do not pay this board. Be back when you said, and do not bring the yard in on your hose a second time.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will be back after one. The afternoon is not mine to spend at the Theatre.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Five is a dark hour. I will keep the broth hot against the jaw, if you want it when you are home between.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The jaw will want it. Leave the crusts in the crock.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mark me. If you write between your goings, write at this table. I will not have papers on the stair because the latch sticks.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The latch stays as it is. I am not mending it. I have a kitchen to write, and the margin of it is empty.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: A kitchen in a play. Do they eat, in that kitchen?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are sent for cooks. A father gives orders he cannot stop giving. Someone calls for baked meats. That is as far as the leaf goes. No one has found a pause in it yet.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then it is a house, and a house is my business more than yours. Eat the broth before it skins over.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am eating it. It is salt and it is hot, and it asks nothing of the left side.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The brush is done. The hem will pass, if nobody kneels down to stare at it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nobody will kneel. Thank you.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The hall candle is for the evening, and you will not be here to burn it at five. When you are back for good, upstairs is your own candle, not mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know whose candle is whose, Mistress.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib has the warm chair. I am not moving a cat for the sake of a cloak.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him. A cat is not in the Shrew this afternoon, and neither am I.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then go at your hour. Do not come home talking of a Christmas sum. I have heard the parish talk of the season already, and none of it was money a body could count.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have no sum to bring you. If one is offered me today, I will not write it down.
